chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
If you say 'It is upon me for Allah,' its expiation is the expiation of an oath.

key_terms.كَفَّارَةُ يَمِينٍ: The expiation required for breaking an oath
key_terms.كَفَّارَتُهُ: Expiation or atonement for a religious obligation or vow
key_terms.يَمِينٍ: Oath, specifically a solemn promise invoking God's name

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking a vow made by saying 'It is upon me for Allah'?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), clarifying that the specific phrasing 'Alayya lillah' triggers the standard expiation for oaths rather than a distinct vow penalty. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on linguistic precision in determining whether a statement constitutes a binding vow (nadhr) or an oath (yamin), ensuring the believer fulfills their obligation with the correct ritual compensation.
